proof_summary: Letting \(d=D(n)\), the facts \(d\le n\) and \(n\equiv d\pmod 9\) give \(n=d+9q\); eventual periodicity of powers of \(10\) modulo \(d\) constructs \(n\) distinct positive exponents whose powers sum to a multiple of \(d\), starting with \(d\) congruent powers and repeatedly replacing one power by ten higher congruent powers to increase the count by nine. The resulting number \(k\), a sum of those distinct powers of \(10\), has digit sum exactly \(n\), is divisible by \(D(n)\), and satisfies \(k\ge 10n>n\), so it is a distinct amicable partner.
